name: Pro Con Challenge

topic.label: Topic
topic.hint: The student picks it: the CX, LD or PF topic, or one bill from the Congress docket. Pro and Con use the same topic.

prompts: Did the Pro speech make a clear case for the topic?
Did the Con speech make a clear case against it?
Were both sides argued with equal care?
Was the evidence clear and fair?

tags.label: Pro case
tags.strength: Your Pro speech made a clear case for the topic.
tags.toWork: Give the Pro speech one clear main reason, and back it up.

tags.label: Con case
tags.strength: Your Con speech made a clear case against the topic.
tags.toWork: Give the Con speech one clear main reason, and back it up.

tags.label: Balance
tags.strength: You argued both sides with the same care.
tags.toWork: Give the weaker side as much work as the side you prefer.

tags.label: Evidence
tags.strength: Your facts and examples were clear and fair.
tags.toWork: Add stronger facts or examples, and say where they come from.

tags.label: Delivery
tags.strength: Your voice and pace were easy to listen to.
tags.toWork: Vary your voice and pace so key lines stand out.

notVerified: Grace length: the rule names a grace period past the 10:30 limit but does not say how long it is. The rules profile holds the grace (docs/events/VENN.md §6 item 17).
Material: 'read from a script' comes from our own summary in docs/events/EVENTS.md §4, not a second read of the rule.
Whether Pro Con Challenge runs at Nationals 2027 (docs/events/CATALOG.md).
source: NSDA High School Unified Manual v2027.1.2, 2026-27 season, Pro Con Challenge rules 1 to 3, as checked in docs/events/VENN.md §6: one 10:30 limit covers both runs; no minimum time for a run; the student picks the topic. Summarized in our own words; no rule text copied.
